tara: Heads-up, started onboarding ceres-7b for quant experiments (GPTQ, AWQ, int8, fp8). quick smoke on CUDA18 nodes shows weird perf + correctness divergence.
ben: what kind of divergence? perf or logits/accuracy?
tara: both. int8/AWQ perf looks fine but GPTQ outputs are shifted on some prompts (few-token hallucination). saving examples.
olga: can you paste an example? also which runtime? trt-llm, vllm, or plain torch?
tara: example below (trimmed):
```
Input: "Summarize the policy changes in plain english."
GPTQ: "The policy increases credits and removes ..."  <-- wrong entity
AWQ/FP8: "The policy clarifies eligibility and updates ..."  <-- correct
```
Runtime: trt-llm on CUDA18 driver stack (nvidia-driver 555, cudatoolkit 12.5 -> constrained env).
ryan: hmm we saw a cudadevrt/nvrtc mismatch on CUDA18 earlier. any relevant warnings in logs?
tara: yes, when launching trt-llm container we got this repeatedly: 
```
[trt-llm] WARN: plugin symbol 'getPluginRegistry' not found, falling back to cpu path
[trt-llm] ERROR: serialized engine version mismatch: expected 4, got 3
```
and vllm backend produced: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
```
ben: those are red flags. Could be kernels compiled with different NVCC/nvrtc. Did the GPTQ artifact include precompiled kernels?
tara: GPTQ wheel includes prebuilt fused kernels. AWQ path uses pure-Python kernels + JIT.
olga: that explains why AWQ runs but GPTQ falls back. prebuilt kernels need exact CUDA/nvrtc ABI. On CUDA18 we changed the system nvrtc -> 18.0, so any binary built against 17.x will crash.
ben: can we repro on a matching container (build GPTQ from source with our CUDA toolchain)? Also check `nvidia-smi` and `nvcc --version`.
ryan: repro steps I used:
1) spawn cuda18 h100 machine image (AMI: rwn-infer-cuda18-h100)
2) pull trt-llm:latest and attach ceres-7b gptq artifact
3) run `python -m trtllm.server --model ceres-7b-gptq`
Observed same symbol error. Building GPTQ from source gave fewer symbol errors but still produced a few kernel launch failures.
tara: important note: perf counters show 30% slowdown on first tokens when fallback to CPU kernels happens. but after warmup it improves, so some parts use optimized paths.
olga: candidate plan: (a) rebuild GPTQ kernels in our cuda18 builder images, (b) validate with trt-llm test harness, (c) add runtime check to our onboarding script to warn if binary-kernel ABI mismatch.
ben: +1. also add a quick accuracy diff check: run our 100-shot eval set (LLMQA-lite) across quant variants and compute delta on exact-match and rouge-l. If delta > threshold, block rollout.
ci-bot: build started: rwn/cpp-gptq:cuda18-2026-03-19 (job 4821). Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/4821
ci-bot: job 4821 failed in step "compile_kernels": nvrtc: unresolved symbol: cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain
ryan: that symbol unresolved often means wrong libcuda.so being picked up at link time. Are we binding host driver into container or using NVIDIA container runtime?
tara: we mount host /usr/lib64/libcuda.so to avoid mismatch (old pattern). with new driver layout on CUDA18 this broke. fallback now is to let container use nvidia-container-toolkit to provide libs.
olga: action items:
- tara: collect 5 failing prompts + traces and upload to /mnt/ci-artifacts/ceres7b/gptq-regressions
- ryan: try building GPTQ kernels in our cuda18 builder and create a test image (ETA today EOD)
- ben: add gating eval to onboarding script that runs small accuracy/latency checks and fails early
- olga: add runtime ABI check (nvrtc/cuda version) and friendly error message in trt-llm startup

tara: one more weirdness: on one node trt-llm reported successful TensorRT engine build but outputs still mismatched vs AWQ. diffing attention weights showed nan/inf in some heads during fp16->int8 conversion.
ben: that could be quant calibration issue during INT8 path. Did we use per-channel calibration?
tara: default is per-tensor for this artifact. switching to per-channel reduced the mismatch but didn't eliminate GPTQ delta.
ryan: possibly mixed problem: ABI mismatch + calibration differences. prioritize getting kernels buildable inside cuda18 and repeat calibration sweep.
ci-bot: build 4828 (rwn/cpp-gptq:cuda18-rebuild) queued.
olga: note for release: document that precompiled GPTQ artifacts are pinned to CUDA/nvrtc minor versions. we need either multiple builds or switch to source-build distribution.
tara: thanks. I'll post the failing sample corpus and update the onboarding PR with gating failures.
ben: assign to me for triage once artifacts are up.
ryan: I'll try vLLM fallback test too; if vllm+AWQ matches expected outputs, we can offer a temporary runtime fallback.
tara: :thumbsup:
